2.translation: In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed. For file-based examples, first extract the [input bundle](⟦shared:0⟧) so the working directory contains ⟦shared:1⟧.

31.translation: The bundled example stores the original annotated strand in ⟦shared:0⟧. For your own imported GFF3 records, use their ⟦shared:1⟧ directly.

33.translation: Input coordinates are 1-based and inclusive. For example, 10 through 12 covers three bases. Gene intervals carry direction in ⟦shared:0⟧. Link intervals can encode direction in ascending or descending endpoint order, so preserve the order at each end after import.

34.translation: Continue to [Plotting concepts](⟦shared:0⟧), or see [Input formats and conversion](⟦shared:1⟧) when reading files.

35.translation: The BLAST-style fields reflect ggchord’s origins in alignment visualization. Query and subject use q/s prefixes, and custom IDs are accepted. See [alignment inputs](⟦shared:0⟧) for actual BLAST rows.

37.translation: A backbone needs unique ⟦shared:0⟧ and complete ⟦shared:1⟧; DNA defaults to bp. Link ⟦shared:2⟧/⟦shared:3⟧ and feature ⟦shared:0⟧ refer to those same identifiers. Use the three small tables above for a [minimal plot](⟦shared:4⟧) before reading file import, cleaning, hierarchy or projection details.

38.translation: For existing files, choose a path by [input and goal](⟦shared:0⟧). Consult the following details as needed, retaining original inputs and repair copies.

40.translation: Nucleotide tables may omit the unit column and use bp. A complete protein length table declares ⟦shared:0⟧. A plot uses one unit. See [protein alignments](⟦shared:1⟧) for full inputs and figures.

42.translation:
Genomic coordinates are **one-based, inclusive bp**. BED/PAF readers convert their
source conventions; do not convert twice. Gene endpoints are ordered with
strand stored separately; link endpoint order may encode direction. A one-bp
link without direction evidence stays unknown. Generic features retain unknown
strand. The legacy ⟦shared:0⟧ default is an exception: ⟦shared:1⟧
converts it to ⟦shared:2⟧ while retaining ⟦shared:3⟧. Use explicit
⟦shared:4⟧ and ⟦shared:5⟧ to retain unknown strand.

43.translation:
Protein backbones use native aa coordinates; see [protein alignments](⟦shared:0⟧). Use [CDS projection](⟦shared:1⟧) to place protein intervals on nucleotide backbones.
Native Cartesian layout units, genomic bp, angles in degrees, physical mm and
track value units are different domains. See the full
[data contract](⟦shared:2⟧).

45.translation: Run this repository-only example from its root. Original files are not rewritten.

48.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ retains record/feature provenance and segmented locations.
⟦shared:1⟧ and ⟦shared:2⟧ retain their conversion metadata. ⟦shared:3⟧,
⟦shared:4⟧ and ⟦shared:5⟧ adapt supported S4 objects; provide
full lengths and IDs explicitly when the object lacks them. ⟦shared:6⟧ and ⟦shared:7⟧ both accept path vectors or globs; repeated resolved paths
are read once in first-occurrence order. Choose one clear entry for a workflow. Missing sequence or
homology data must be supplied by the analyst, not invented by the plotting layer.

52.translation:
Validation reports issues; cleaning makes explicit repairs with a report.
Preparation combines workflow steps without inferring biological membership.
Inspect ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ and ⟦shared:2⟧ before plotting.
⟦shared:3⟧ in geometry refers to the resolved layer input, while ⟦shared:4⟧
means a physical file line; GenBank has separate record/feature provenance.
Aggregates may have ⟦shared:5⟧ and ⟦shared:6⟧ flags. Preserve these
when filtering or merging links.

53.translation: ## Inspect a problematic input and its repair report ⟦shared:0⟧

56.translation:
The demonstration intentionally includes an unknown ID and
identity outside 0–100 in copied source rows. These explicit repairs are not a recommendation to clip
scientific observations silently. Inspect ⟦shared:0⟧ and ⟦shared:1⟧,
retain the original table, and choose policies appropriate to actual evidence.
A legitimate reverse alignment can keep endpoint order instead of being sorted.
⟦shared:2⟧ therefore retains its workflow-specific default policy;
standalone cleaning and preparation should not be assumed identical.

60.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ summarizes declared membership without concatenating contigs.
No membership is inferred from an accession prefix. Provide globally unique IDs
when separate samples reuse local contig names. Use [file formats and adapters](⟦shared:1⟧)
for format/optional-object details, and the [real-record manual](⟦shared:2⟧)
to carry reports into a complete figure.

63.translation:
The second positional constructor argument is ⟦shared:0⟧, not ⟦shared:1⟧.
Use explicit argument names as in the shared examples. Optional identity, length
and coverage fields are needed only by operations that consume them. See
[standard BLAST/protein input](⟦shared:2⟧) and [parameter formats](⟦shared:3⟧).

65.translation: Input IDs must match complete sequence records. Keep original records separate from repaired copies. Decreasing endpoints can be legitimate reverse hits; warnings do not all mean rows must be removed.

68.translation:
This chapter uses bundled sequence lengths, observed HSPs and source-strand
annotations. ⟦shared:0⟧ is a common annotation source. Generic feature layers
inherit the whole table; default gene layers require explicit gene/CDS classes.
An explicit layer table or data function takes priority. Use disjoint subsets
when combining the two kinds of geometry.
